headline: Insulin degludec
punch: Why it is on a height list, and why that is dangerous.

headline: What it actually is
body: An ultra-long basal insulin analogue. It forms soluble multi-hexamer depots under the skin that dissociate slowly, giving an extremely flat, peakless profile rather than a curve. | Mean terminal half-life **25 hours**, roughly twice insulin glargine's 12.1. Duration of action beyond **42 hours**. Steady state after about **3 days**, with 4 times lower day-to-day variability than glargine.

headline: Why it appears here
body: Portal insulin, meaning insulin reaching the liver, **stimulates hepatic GH-receptor synthesis and its translocation to the cell surface**. Without adequate portal insulin the liver cannot fully respond to GH. | So insulin is upstream of the entire IGF-1 response. This is a real mechanism and it is why insulin keeps appearing in GH discussions.
punch: Insulin decides whether your liver can hear GH.

headline: How large that effect is
body: Take 17 type 1 diabetics off basal insulin for **8 hours**: IGFBP-1 rose from **32 to 205 ng/mL** and free IGF-1 fell **below the detection limit in 15 of 17**. | Give one dose back and free IGF-1 rebounded to **0.54 ng/mL** within two hours. The axis tracks insulin on a timescale of hours, in both directions.
punch: _Restoring insulin restored free IGF-1 within hours._

headline: Read that evidence carefully
body: Every one of those numbers comes from people who were **insulin deficient** and had it restored. That is the entire evidence base for insulin and the IGF-1 axis. | It shows that going from not enough insulin to normal insulin fixes the axis. It does not show that going from normal to extra does anything further, and nobody has run that experiment.
punch: ==Restoring a deficiency is not the same as adding a surplus.==

headline: The actual risk
body: A 30-year-old bodybuilder injected 70 IU of short-acting insulin before a competition to stimulate GH. He lost consciousness, convulsed, required intubation, and **glucose infusion alone was not enough to stabilise him**. It took additional glucose plus glucagon in intensive care. | That was a short-acting insulin. Degludec has a 25-hour half-life and over 42 hours of action, so a mistake cannot be waited out.
punch: A 42-hour mistake cannot be corrected by waiting.

headline: Why the profile matters
body: Insulin has what the pharmacology literature plainly calls **a narrow therapeutic window**. Degludec's flatness is a genuine safety advantage for a diabetic who needs stable baseline coverage. | For someone with a working pancreas it is the opposite: a continuous, inescapable insulin floor layered on top of their own regulated supply, for most of two days per injection.
punch: The feature that makes it safe in diabetes makes it worse here.

headline: There is no counter
body: For the usual downsides I give you what offsets them. Here there is not one that the evidence supports, and pretending otherwise would be dishonest. | Carbohydrate timing reduces hypoglycaemia risk but does not eliminate it across a 42-hour window, and it does not address the fact that no trial has shown added insulin raises IGF-1 in someone who already makes enough.
punch: _No evidence-based mitigation exists for this use._

headline: What would change this
body: The study that would justify it is simple to describe: give basal insulin to non-diabetic adolescents with normal insulin and measure free IGF-1 and height against placebo. | It has not been done. Until it is, the mechanism is real and the application rests on extrapolating from insulin-deficient patients to insulin-sufficient ones.
punch: The mechanism is proven. The use is not.

headline: Where the real lever is
body: The most interesting insulin result is about route rather than amount. Switching patients from subcutaneous to **intraperitoneal** delivery, which reaches the liver first, dropped IGFBP-1 by **100.7 µg/L**, p < 0.01, with no relationship to HbA1c change. | So hepatic exposure is what moves this axis, and subcutaneous injection is the route that delivers least of it to the liver.
punch: Route beat dose. Subcutaneous is the wrong route for this.

headline: Verdict
body: Real mechanism, excellent drug for its licensed purpose, and the weakest risk-to-evidence ratio of anything in this axis for the use people want it for. | The human data shows restoring deficient insulin restores IGF-1. It does not show adding insulin to a working pancreas does anything, and the failure mode is a hypoglycaemic event you cannot sleep off.
punch: Proven mechanism. Unproven use. Unforgiving kinetics.
